Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the recap and the attachments. A few quick notes from us: 

- PII scope: We treat unredacted payment card data and full SSNs as prohibited. Customer identifiers (email, customer_id) and hashed identifiers are allowed but must be handled as sensitive and logged accordingly.
- Retention: For conversation transcripts we typically require 90 days; for audit logs we need 12 months. We may request longer retention for certain regulatory workflows.
- Audit logs: We need request/response metadata, timestamps, user-id, and indicators of whether PII was redacted. Token-level logging is acceptable if redaction is enforced - need to confirm.
- Residency: Primary requirement is US (multi-region is okay but must guarantee no egress outside US without approval).
- Support access/break-glass: We need a documented, auditable workflow including approvals from our security on a per-incident basis.

Can you confirm whether break-glass access generates an immutable entry with the approver and justification? Also, for RBAC, we'd like a matrix of default roles + privileges that we can map to our internal roles (ops, platform, security).

If possible, can Neha pick a couple of available times tomorrow for the technical deep-dive? Alexis (CC) will coordinate with our security team.

Best,
Samantha
Head of Platform Partnerships, FinTechCorp
samantha.lee@fintechcorp.com

Thanks Samantha, great questions. Quick answers inline, plus a suggested agenda for the technical session.

Inline answers:
- Break-glass audit: Yes, every emergency access event triggers an immutable audit record that includes: timestamp, Redwood operator identity, requested scope, approver identity (customer-side or delegated approver), justification text, and a link to the captured session logs. The record cannot be modified; it's retained per the configured audit retention policy. Details are in break_glass_playbook.docx.
- RBAC matrix: The attached redwood_rbac_matrix_v2.xlsx contains default role mappings. High level:
  - Admin: full config + billing + user management (limited to customer-designated admins)
  - Platform/Operator: deploy/manage models, scale pools, but no billing or KMS key export
  - Support-Incident: scoped access to request logs and session replay for a specific incident; access requires explicit coin-approval (see playbook)
  - Read-Only: dashboards, metrics, and audit logs (no object download)

- Residency: Redwood supports region pinning for Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we can pin data to US regions only and restrict egress. We'll include the exact region SLA in the contract addendum.

Technical session suggested agenda (30-45m):
1) Neha: RBAC role walkthrough + demo of scoped support access (10m)
2) Neha: Break-glass flow and audit evidence (10m)
3) Team Q&A / mapping to your internal roles (10-15m)

Neha, can you propose 2 time slots tomorrow morning PT? Also add token-level logging and KMS notes below if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi all,

Two proposed slots tomorrow (Wed): 2026-05-20 09:00-09:45 PT or 2026-05-20 11:00-11:45 PT. Please confirm which works for the FinTechCorp security team.

Technical clarifications to supplement Marissa's note:
- Token-level logging: By default we log request/response metadata and redaction flags. We can enable token-level logs for specific deployments but redact or hash tokens deemed PII. If you enable token logs for debugging, those logs are stored encrypted at rest and can be forward-swept to your SIEM via secure transfer; retention is configurable (defaults: 30 days for token logs, 365 days for audit logs).
- Encryption/KMS: All customer data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed keys (KMS) in Dedicated/Private. For hosted customers, we support customer-managed KMS via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault integrations. Key export is disabled.
- Support access workflow: Support-incident role is strictly scoped to a ticket/incident ID. Break-glass requires:
  1) Customer-approved approver (could be a security on-call) to confirm the emergency
  2) A short justification entered into the system by the Redwood operator
  3) Two-factor signoff (Redwood operator + customer approver)
  4) Immutable audit record + session capture link stored in the evidence bucket

I attached a short excerpt from the playbook in the drive link and updated the RBAC matrix with the incident-scoped permission row.

Happy to demo the session capture and show the immutable log during the meeting.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
